newsitem.title: UK: IFC emerging market index hits another new high.
newsitem.headline: IFC emerging market index hits another new high.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation's composite index of emerging market equities, denominated in dollars, continued this week's gains, adding 0.4 percent to 320.55 at the start of play on Friday.
The index has been breaking its 1997 highs all week and it's Friday opening level represents the latest high.
Latin America edged down 0.2 percent day-on-day to 596.07, Asia was up 0.1 percent at 262.96, and Europe, Middle East and Africa were up 1.8 percent at 155.42.
The IFC composite index began 1997 at 294.37, after making gains of 7.0 percent over the course of 1996.
ING Barings' Global Emerging Market Index (BEMI), also denominated in dollars, was up 0.29 percent day-on-day at 173.84 at 1130 GMT, a new high.
It began 1997 at 159.57 after rising 8.9 percent over the course of 1996.
Morgan Stanley's dollar-denominated Emerging Markets Free index was up 0.33 percent at 516.115, calculated after the close of trade on Thursday.
It began 1997 at 476.315 after making gains of 3.9 percent over 1996. Its 1997 high of 508.674 was also reached on January 20.

All indices are capitalisation-weighted and are calculated daily. The IFC index measures returns on equities, liquid and accessible to foreign investors, from 30 emerging market countries after adding Russia, Slovakia, Egypt and Morocco on February 3. It is updated at 2300 GMT.
The BEMI index measures equity returns without dividends from some 21 emerging market countries, with the latest changes reported by 0900 GMT.
The MSCI Free measures equity returns without dividends from 26 emerging market nations. Changes are reported at 1300 GMT.
The J.P. Morgan emerging market bond index ELMI, its returns calculated in dollar terms, rose 0.02 percent to 126.44 by the start of trade on Friday, another 1997 high.
It began 1997 at 124.83 after making gains of 14.86 percent over 1996.
By region, Latin America was up 0.02 percent at 105.20, Asia fell 0.04 to 132.28 and East Europe was up 0.02 at 161.21.
